category_title: Students with reactive study habits and entity-based beliefs about academic ability
scenario_title: Post-exam reflection and study habit review
minimal_context: During a peer fellow study session, the tutor asks the student to reflect on their recent Biology exam results to determine the causes of their academic difficulty.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's take some time in our peer fellow session today to reflect on the recent Biology exam results and determine the causes of any difficulties you might have had.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I got my grade back and it's really disappointing. I studied the night before the exam and took breaks while studying, but I guess I can't do this. I'm not a Biology person.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: What other study habits did you use to prepare for the exam?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I usually study alone primarily. But really, the professor talks too fast. The test didn't cover the lectures in class.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: How do you plan to prepare for the next exam?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: She doesn't teach, care, or want us to pass, so I'm not going to. Everyone agrees with me. I'm just not smart enough.

dialogue_combined:

TUTOR: How do you plan to prepare for the next exam?

task.content: Reflecting on disappointing Biology exam results and determining the causes of academic difficulty
task.learning_goal: Respond to test grades with more productive behaviors, not merely react to them with disappointment

context.materials: Anonymous everyday data survey results, graphical representations of study habits posted on the course's online homepage
context.social_setting: Group discussions during peer fellow sessions

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: After receiving disappointing exam results in a gateway course like Biology
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Circulating scripted beliefs about why they did poorly, engaging in fearful and unproductive conversations, and claiming the professor doesn't teach or care so they are not going to try
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Entity-based beliefs about academic ability, confirmation bias, and feeling that grades are beyond their control
related_quotes: The test didn't cover the lectures in class
I can't do this. I'm not a math (or Biology or Chemistry) person
He's too difficult to understand and everyone agrees with me
She [the professor] doesn't teach, care, or want us to pass, so I'm not going to

behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Leaning on breaks 92% of the time, studying the day of or the night before their exams, and studying alone primarily
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Unaware of cognitive biases and relying on shallow study strategies
